Appendix A

Glossary

Definitions run alphabetically letter by letter, ignoring spaces, case and punctuation; digits sort first. Numbers locate chapters defining or relying on terms, in book order; passing mentions are omitted.

A

Abliteration
Editing model weights without further training to remove a refusal pattern found by comparing internal responses to harmful and harmless prompts.07
ACID atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability
Database transaction guarantees. Atomicity: all changes happen or none do. Consistency: declared constraints hold after commit. Isolation: the chosen level controls which concurrency anomalies are prevented. Durability: committed data survives a crash. Postgres with pgvector lets a memory row and its vector commit together.0811
Agentic search
Agent-directed retrieval using grep, glob and file reads, checking results and searching again. It needs no index and sees current files, but costs tool calls and depends on the agent's judgment.0005
AGENTS.md
A repository-root Markdown file coding agents load for project instructions, an open convention described as "a README for agents".0102
ANN approximate nearest neighbor
Search returning near vectors without checking every vector, using indexes such as HNSW or IVFFlat. Results can differ from exact search, trading recall for speed.081119
AOF append-only file
Redis's rewritable on-disk recovery record represents current data rather than every original command. Fsync forces writes to storage: always (every write), everysec (about once a second) or no (the operating system decides).09
Apache AGE
A Postgres extension that runs openCypher graph queries.0814
API application programming interface
The interface for calling another program, such as a hosted model or memory service.0013
Archival memory
In Letta, memory outside the context window, read through a search tool. Blocks stay in context.0001
Asterisk
An open-source PBX that Chapters 22 and 23 propose as the phone switch between carrier and local speech software. Neither runs it.2223
AudioSocket
An Asterisk protocol that streams raw audio (PCM, pulse-code modulation) over a socket to a local program, here a proposed Pipecat worker (see Pipecat).2223
Audit trail
An append-only record for later review: who read or changed which record, when and under which rule.08172223

B

BAA business associate agreement
A written agreement with an outside party that handles protected health information for a US health provider. Chapter 22 says to check each vendor's data flow to see if one is needed.22
Bead
A Beads work item: title, status, owner and links to blocking items.01
Beads bd
A coding-agent task tracker storing work items as a dependency graph, showing blocked and ready items and their owners.0112
BEAM
A memory benchmark of 100 conversations up to 10 million tokens, with 2,000 validated questions. Its authors report that models with 1 million tokens of context degrade as dialogues grow.16
BFCL Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard
A tool-calling benchmark. Chapter 06 cites BFCL-V4 scores for small models.06
bfloat16, float16 and float32
Weight and vector formats: float32 takes 4 bytes per number, float16 and bfloat16 take 2. bfloat16 keeps float32's exponent range with fewer precision bits; float16 has a narrower range. Chapter 03 checks which formats EmbeddingGemma 2 supports; FP8 is an 8-bit float taking 1 byte.000304
BGE-M3
An embedding model that produces dense, sparse and multi-vector output, with an 8192-token input.0305
Binary quantization
Keeping one bit per vector number, so the packed values alone are 32 times smaller than 32-bit numbers, before scales or metadata. Recall loss varies with model and data, so stores usually rescore with retained full vectors.0311
Bitemporal
Keeping valid time and recorded time for each fact. Also called "two timelines" (Chapter 14) and "both clocks" (Chapters 22 and 23). See Valid time and Recorded time.142223
BM25
A keyword scoring formula. It rewards rare query words with diminishing returns for repeats and adjusts for note length.000512
Both clocks
See Bitemporal.

C

Cache
A fast, disposable copy of recomputable data, keyed until expiry or eviction. Never keep the only copy there; recompute misses or doubtful entries from the source.0010
Cache key
A cache-entry label including every result-changing input: model version, parameters, prompt version and user scope. Example: emb:sha256(canonical_JSON([tenant, model_revision, parameters, prompt_version, text])) hashes a canonical JSON array, avoiding ambiguous field joins.10
Candidate pool
The top N results of the first searches. Later steps only reorder or trim it, so pool recall caps subsequent stages.05061319
Cartridges
A research method that trains a small KV cache for a corpus once instead of prompting with it. Its authors report using 1/38.6 as much memory as in-context learning at matched quality; a small test in Chapter 16 kept the memory saving but lost accuracy.0016
CC-BY-NC Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial
A license, used by models such as Jina v5, that allows noncommercial use only; commercial use needs separate permission.0305
Checkpoint
Four meanings. 1. Agent framework (Chapters 00, 13, 15, 17): a saved snapshot of a run's state, for resuming. 2. Model (Chapters 06, 07, 16): a saved set of weights. 3. Event log (Chapter 17): a worker's saved position. 4. SQLite (Chapter 12): copying the write-ahead log into the main file. See also Checkpoint fork.0006071213151617
Checkpointer
Saves agent state after each step, keyed by thread id, for conversation resumption.1517
Checkpoint fork
Starting branches from one saved checkpoint. Each branch keeps its own draft memory; trusted application code promotes only approved facts to the shared Store. Replaying a checkpoint rewinds neither the Store nor an external action. See Chapter 13, Forked planning.1317
Chunk chunking
A note, document or conversation segment embedded and stored as one unit. Where you cut decides what can be found.0305
CLAUDE.md
A hand-written instruction file that Claude Code loads at the start of every conversation, as a user message after the system prompt: the simplest always-loaded memory.0001
CMB Coding Memory Benchmark
A coding-memory benchmark with separate diagnostic question-answering and execution-graded code-editing tracks. Retrieval recall, QA score and task resolution measure different things; never subtract one from another.16
CoALA
A paper that splits a language agent's memory into four kinds: working, episodic, semantic and procedural.00
Code-linked freshness
Storing the file, symbol and commit that each fact about code was true at, and re-checking or suppressing the fact when that code changes.01
Cognee
A memory framework that uses a model to extract facts into a knowledge graph, with a vector index beside it.1314
ColBERT
A retrieval model family built on late interaction (one vector per token). ColBERTv2 compresses to cut the extra storage.0405
Cold start
The first call after a service starts, while the model and database load.0619
Collection
A named vector-store record group. Isolation and filtering depend on the store; test that one credential cannot read another collection.11
ColPali and the ColQwen family
Multi-vector models that keep one vector per visual patch of a page image. Their authors introduced ViDoRe to argue that embedding page images beats OCR. See Multi-vector.04
Community summary
A model-written summary of a closely linked entity cluster.14
Compaction
Shrinking a long conversation by summarizing or dropping older turns so it fits the context window.16
Compiled page
A Markdown page the agent wrote from sources, such as a summary, entity, concept or comparison.02
Consolidation
After-turn work: merging duplicates, summarizing old episodes into facts and settling contradictions.001316
Constrained decoding
Decoding that permits only tokens consistent with a grammar or supported schema. Check that generation finished before parsing; a valid shape does not make the facts correct.0607
Consumer group
Distributes new Redis stream entries among workers and tracks acknowledgment. A crash after acting but before acknowledging lets another worker claim and repeat the action; make processing idempotent.09
Context database
A system that keeps files unchanged and adds a model-written summary to each directory, so an agent can browse a tree and read summaries at two sizes before opening a file. OpenViking is the example.000218
Context engineering
Anthropic's name for curating the tokens a model sees at inference time. Chapter 16 places the memory tool, editing and compaction under it.1516
Context rot
The drop in a model's reliability as input grows. Chroma reported it across 18 models, even on a trivial repeat-the-text task.0016
Contextual Retrieval
At write time an LLM writes 50 to 100 tokens placing a chunk in its document. That text is prepended to the chunk before the chunk is embedded and, separately, indexed for BM25.05
Context window
A model's maximum usable token span. Earlier messages outside it are directly visible only if the application resupplies them.000615
Continuous batching
Adds and removes requests at every decoding step, letting one GPU serve many calls. Chapters 22 and 23 propose it for vLLM serving; neither runs it.2223
Cosine similarity
The normalized dot product of non-zero vectors: -1 means opposite directions, 0 orthogonal, 1 identical directions. Similar texts usually score high, not necessarily 1.0309
CRM customer relationship management
The system that holds customer records and contact history.212223
Cross-encoder
A model scoring the relevance of a query and note read together. Most rerankers are cross-encoders.05
Crypto-shredding
Making data unreadable by destroying its encryption key. It works only if every relevant copy is encrypted under that key.17
CVE common vulnerabilities and exposures
A public identifier for a known security flaw. Chapter 17 cites two in LangGraph's SQLite checkpointer, Chapter 08 one in pgvector's IVFFlat index build.0817
Cypher
Neo4j's query language for matching node and edge patterns. openCypher is its open specification, used by Apache AGE and FalkorDB.0814

D

Data residency
A rule or design that keeps a region's personal data, models and keys on servers in that region. Chapter 23 designs five isolated data regions.23
Dead-letter queue
A durable place that keeps events whose retries ran out, with event id, attempt count and error, so operators can repair the cause and submit again.17
Dense vector
One fixed-length vector of floating-point or quantized numbers per item. It matches overall meaning and is usually much smaller than a multi-vector one.0305
Dimension
A vector's length in numbers. Models tested in Chapter 03 output 384 to 4,096 numbers per text; other models differ.030811
Directed persistence fixture
A test in which the harness directs the model's tool edits to prove save, recall, resume and delete work. It does not test autonomous extraction quality or the minimum model or GPU.1318
DiskANN
A graph index like HNSW designed for SSD, so it can exceed RAM but is slower per hop.0811
Distillation
Training a small model to imitate a larger one. Chapters 06 and 07 note community uploads called distills; read their base model and procedure from the model card.0607
Document id
A stored-note key. Chapter 19's save replaces that id's note; other APIs distinguish insert, update and upsert.19
DolphinBench
A benchmark (September 2026) of knowledge-work tasks over three personas, each with about 500K tokens of user messages. Submissions report completion, total cost and latency.1617
Dolt
A SQL database with git-style commits, branches and remotes. Beads stores its items in it.01
Dream
In Anthropic's Managed Agents, a research-preview job that reads a memory store and past transcripts, then writes a reorganized memory store.16

E

EHR electronic health record
A practice's clinical record system. Chapter 22 keeps one underneath as the system of record, which the memory layer never replaces.22
Embedding
A learned numerical representation of an input, such as text, an image or audio. Retrieval models are trained to place matching inputs near each other.000304
Embedding inversion
Turning a vector back into its text. Chapter 17 cites exact recovery of 92% of 32-token inputs for GTR-base and 60.9% for a hosted encoder (paper figures, not run here), so a vector index is not anonymized.17
Embedding model embedder
A model turning text or other input into embeddings. It answers nothing and remembers nothing; the store holds the memory.030406
Embedding space
An embedding model's learned coordinate system. Do not mix vectors from different models, revisions or preprocessing in one index unless the vendor documents a shared space.030408
Encoder
A neural network mapping input tokens to representations. Bidirectional text encoders use context on both sides; retrieval models may combine token vectors or keep several. Decoder (left-to-right) embedders can instead use the final token's vector.03
Entity linking
Mapping a text mention to an entity record. Chapter 13 covers Mem0 v3 entity signals. See Entity resolution for duplicate detection.0613
Entity resolution
Deciding whether entity records represent the same thing; a mistake can merge two people into one graph node. See Entity linking for attaching mentions.17
Episode
Raw input, such as a conversation turn, retained as the source for extracted entities and facts.081314
Episodic memory
What happened, in order, with times, usually held in an append-only log such as JSONL or an event table.0012
E-signature levels
Laws such as EU eIDAS distinguish advanced from qualified electronic signatures; a qualified one has the effect of a handwritten signature. Chapter 23 leaves the level for each document to counsel.23
Event log
A durable, append-only record of accepted changes and deletions, from which searchable memory is derived and rebuilt.12171821
EverOS
A self-run, Apache-2.0 memory system that keeps readable Markdown as the canonical source, with SQLite and LanceDB indexes, user and agent tracks and offline reflection. Surveyed in Chapter 13, not run.1318
Eviction
A cache removing items before they expire to free memory, as Redis policies such as allkeys-lru do.0910
Exact search
Search guaranteed to return the nearest neighbors under the chosen distance. By default, pgvector scans eligible rows; latency grows with table size.0811
Extraction
Turning raw conversation into short, separate facts or entities.061314

F

FalkorDB
A property graph database that uses openCypher and speaks the Redis protocol.14
Fencing token
See Lease.
Fine-tuning
Further training that changes a model's behavior. A compliant fine-tune is an alternative to weight editing (abliteration) for reducing refusals.0007
FLAT
A Redis vector index type that scans every stored vector, so results are exact. HNSW is the approximate alternative used in Chapter 09.09
Forgetting
Expiring, deleting or superseding records. Without it a store only grows and stale facts surface. See Soft forgetting.00
FP8
See bfloat16, float16 and float32.
Frontmatter
A short block of settings between two --- lines at the top of a Markdown file.01
FTS full-text search
Keyword search over the words in stored text. SQLite's FTS5 and Postgres tsvector with a GIN index are examples.000812
FTS5
SQLite's built-in full-text search module, which indexes words and ranks matches.000512

G

GBNF
A grammar format llama.cpp accepts to force valid output such as JSON.06
GDPR General Data Protection Regulation
The European Union's data protection law. Chapter 23 takes its storage-limitation and erasure rules as engineering inputs for the EU region, not legal advice.23
Generative Agents
A 2023 study that scored each memory by recency, importance and relevance and used periodic reflection to turn observations into higher-level ones.000515
GGUF
A llama.cpp and Ollama model-file format holding weights and metadata. Vision models add a projector file (see Vision projector).020607
GIN generalized inverted index
A Postgres inverted index for composite values, including tsvector words and JSONB keys and values.08
GitHub Copilot Memory
Facts a coding agent writes and GitHub stores. Repository-level facts cite code and are checked when used; user preferences follow one person across repositories.0113
Golden set
A small file of real questions with their answering note ids. Cover real query types: exact lookups, paraphrases and questions with no valid hit.0517
Graphiti
The open-source engine behind Zep. It keeps a temporal graph of episodes, entities and facts with validity windows, invalidating a replaced fact instead of deleting it.001314
GraphRAG
Microsoft's method that extracts entities and relations, groups them into communities and summarizes each, with global, local and DRIFT search (local search expanded through community summaries).14
Graph search
Walking from named entities along the edges between them. It suits multi-hop and time-aware questions.0014
grep, glob
grep searches inside files for text. A glob is a file-name pattern such as src/**/*.ts.0105

H

HaluMem
A benchmark that counts hallucinations at each memory operation: extraction, updating and question answering. It looks for fabricated, wrong, conflicting and missing memories, so it measures memory quality, not task success or security.1617
Harness
Runs the model and returns saved text to its context window.0001
Heretic
Finds weight edits balancing refusal reduction against base-model divergence.07
Hindsight
A memory framework with three calls (see Retain, recall, reflect). It extracts facts and entities with a model and uses Postgres with pgvector as its primary storage.060813
HIPAA Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
The US federal health-privacy law. Chapter 22 treats a permission under it as separate from a telephone-marketing one (TCPA).1622
HippoRAG
Retrieval extracting a corpus entity graph at write time and ranking nodes per query with Personalized PageRank.14
HNSW hierarchical navigable small world
A layered near-neighbor graph, mostly in RAM, searched by node-to-node hops. Fast and accurate but memory-hungry. Chapters 08 and 11 give its settings and compare other indexes.00080911
Honcho
A memory product organized around peers, meaning what one participant knows about another; self-run under AGPL-3.0 or managed.13
Hook
A command a coding tool runs on a lifecycle event, such as a session start or tool call. Memory tools use hooks to capture activity without the model choosing, so audit what they capture.011317
Hot tier
A fast layer, such as Redis, refilled from a durable system-of-record store.09
Hybrid search
Running keyword search and vector search together and merging the two result lists.000508
HyDE hypothetical document embeddings
A method that asks an LLM to write a plausible answer, embeds that answer and searches with it. The invented answer only has to be worded like the real one.05
Hy-Memory
Tencent's Apache-2.0 memory framework with Chat, Working and Coding pipelines. The name also covers a purpose-trained writer model, Hy-Memory-30B-A3B (about 30 billion parameters, 3 billion used per token). Not run.0616

I

Idempotency key
A write identifier recognizing retries as the same request. See Receipt.172223
Idempotent
An operation whose repeated events have the same effect as one.0617
Ingest, query, lint
The three loops of an LLM wiki: add a source, ask a question, check wiki health.02
InjecMEM
Plants a poisoned memory record in one chat turn without store access. Topical cues surface it later; an optimized command inside steers answers.1617
Inject
The final read-path step: place surviving results in context, labeled as data, not instructions.00
Iterative scan
A pgvector setting, available since version 0.8.0, that keeps walking the index until enough rows pass the filter or the scan limits are hit.0811
IVF inverted file
An index scanning only the nearest vector clusters. Low probe counts can beat flat search at scale but miss neighbors in unscanned clusters; high recall can cost more than flat.0811
IVFFlat
pgvector's cluster index. It builds faster and is smaller than HNSW, but the table needs data before you build it. Use pgvector 0.8.7 or later: Chapter 08's pin fixes a CVE in IVFFlat index builds.0819

J

JSONB
A Postgres column type for JSON. It holds per-row attributes, so adding an attribute needs no table change.08
JSONL JSON lines
One JSON object per line in a text file, so appending means writing a new line.0012

K

KL divergence Kullback–Leibler divergence
A number measuring divergence between distributions, here edited versus base next-token probabilities. Heretic uses it to check that an edit barely shifts answers to harmless prompts. It is not a memory-accuracy score.07
KNN k nearest neighbors
The k closest stored vectors: exact with FLAT or sqlite-vec, approximate with an ANN index.0912
Knowledge graph
Memory stored as nodes and edges (see Node, edge); questions are answered by walking the links.14
Known-at recall
Recall of facts whose valid time contains the requested effective date and whose recorded time contains the requested as-known-on date, so a later correction does not rewrite earlier knowledge. Today's retention and access rules still apply.2223
Kuzu
An embedded graph database. Its repository is archived and Graphiti marks its Kuzu driver deprecated, so start nothing new on it.14
KV cache key-value cache
The attention state a model computes for a prompt. Reusing it skips re-reading the prefix. A provider (prompt cache) or local server (see KV-cache offload) can keep it.1016
KV-cache offload
A self-run layer, such as LMCache, that moves a server's KV cache from GPU memory to CPU RAM, disk or remote backends and shares it across requests and engines. It differs from provider prompt caching.10

L

L0, L1, L2
Three levels of one context-database directory. L0 is a one-line abstract and L1 a longer overview, both model-written summaries. L2 is the original or parsed full content, loaded on demand.02
LanceDB
An embedded vector store that keeps versioned Lance tables on disk or object storage.11
LangGraph
An agent framework. Its checkpointers save run state, and its Store keeps JSON documents under a namespace and key.081317
LangMem
Memory extraction tools used with the LangGraph Store. Extraction calls the model you pass in.13
Late chunking
Embedding the whole document with a long-context model, then pooling token vectors per chunk so each carries the surrounding text.05
Late interaction
Keeping one vector per token and comparing query tokens with note tokens. It matches finer detail than one vector per note, at about an order of magnitude more storage (Chapter 05).030511
Lease lock key
A TTL-bound Redis job-holder key. SET lease:<id> <holder_value> NX PX 30000 claims it for 30 seconds using a random holder value. Renew or release only on a matching value, atomically with Lua or equivalent compare-and-set. A stalled worker can outlive its lease. Each grant needs a fencing token: a rising counter. The destination rejects writes below the highest counter seen.09
Legal hold
A reviewed exception retaining records past scheduled deletion. Chapters 22 and 23 assign a human owner and review date; a model never sets or lifts a hold.2223
Letta
A memory framework (also Chapter 00) that keeps labeled memory blocks always in context and a searchable archival memory outside it. The agent edits its own memory with tool calls.010613
LISTEN/NOTIFY
A Postgres feature in which one session sends a NOTIFY on a channel and every session that ran LISTEN on it wakes up.08
llama.cpp
A program that runs GGUF models locally. Its server accepts GBNF grammars and can save a prompt's KV cache to disk.030610
LLM large language model
A language model reading and writing text; here, notes, extracted facts or answers.000205
LLM wiki
A git repository of Markdown pages that an agent writes and updates from source documents. The agent compiles knowledge once and keeps it current instead of rebuilding it per question.0218
LoCoMo
A benchmark of ten very long conversations with question answering, event summarization and dialogue tasks. An independent audit reports incorrect reference answers.0205061314161718
LongMemEval
A benchmark of 500 questions on scalable chat histories, testing extraction, multi-session and temporal reasoning, knowledge updates and abstention.01050613141617
LoRA low-rank adaptation
A small set of trained matrices added to a frozen model, so behavior or knowledge can change without retraining the whole model. Chapter 16 uses it as the baseline for a memory-table paper.16
Lost in the middle
A 2023 study finding that accuracy drops when the relevant fact sits mid-context, even for models built for long inputs.0015
LRU least recently used
A rule for choosing what to evict: the item unused longest goes first. Memcached evicts at the LRU tail.0910

M

Managed cloud memory service
A vendor service that extracts, stores and searches memories, while your application authenticates users and sets scope. Chapter 13 compares Google, AWS and Microsoft Foundry; Chapter 18 says when to pick one. None was run.001318
MaxSim
For each query vector, take its best similarity to any vector of the stored item (page or chunk), then sum those scores as the item's ranking score.0411
MCP Model Context Protocol
The standard for connecting tools to a model. Chapter 13 tests its reference memory server, which keeps a whole-file graph and serializes writes from several processes with a lock.000213
Mem0
A memory framework whose background model extracts short facts into a vector store with one add-only call. Its v3 algorithm (April 2026; see Mem0 v3) scores semantic, keyword and entity signals with time-aware ranking. Keyword and entity scores only rerank what semantic search found, so they cannot recover a missed exact match (Chapter 13).00061317
Mem0 v3
The Mem0 algorithm as shipped in the pinned mem0ai==2.2.1 Python package. The book uses v3 for the algorithm and mem0ai==2.2.1 for the package.0613
MEM1
A research prototype trained with reinforcement learning to reason and consolidate memory together: each turn it merges new observations into one compact state and discards the rest. Code is released.16
MemAgent
A research prototype trained with reinforcement learning to read a long document in segments and overwrite a fixed working memory. It holds state within one task, not user facts across sessions. Code is released.16
Memanto
A memory product with typed memories, context briefings and lifecycle state. The code is MIT-licensed; it runs locally or in the cloud.13
Memcached
A cache server that keeps key/value copies in RAM by default until expiry or eviction. See Cache.0010
MemGen
A research method in which a learned trigger decides when a second module supplies learned internal vectors rather than extra prompt words. Code and checkpoints are released, with limits on supported tasks.16
MemGPT
A 2023 design that pages information between tiers of memory around the context window.1415
Memory (agent)
Every method that chooses which text enters the context window, plus every method that saves new text after a turn.00
MemoryAgentBench
A benchmark of multi-turn tests of accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding and selective forgetting. Of the six benchmarks compared in Chapter 17, only it tests selective forgetting.1617
MemoryArena
A 2026 benchmark of interdependent multi-session tasks in web navigation, planning, search and formal reasoning.1617
Memory block
In Letta, a labeled, size-limited piece of core memory kept in context. The agent edits blocks through tools.010613
Memory framework
A software layer between an agent and its storage. It combines a note-taking model, an embedder and a store, and decides what to write and recall.13
Memory poisoning
Getting false or hostile text saved into an agent's memory for later sessions to read.17
Memory-R1
A research method that uses reinforcement learning to train a Memory Manager, which chooses ADD, UPDATE, DELETE or NOOP, and an Answer Agent. Unlike MemRL, it learns new weights. Chapter 06 gives its LoCoMo evidence and limits.06
Memory Tax
A paper (October 2026) that scores memory systems against naive retrieval over the raw history. A gain over that baseline is the memory benefit; a loss is the memory tax.16
Memory tool
Anthropic's API tool that gives the model a /memories directory. Your code decides where the files live, and Claude checks the directory before starting a task.0001
MemPalace
A local-first, MIT-licensed memory keeping conversations verbatim in scoped wings, rooms and drawers, with a pluggable backend (Chroma by default) and a local SQLite temporal graph with validity windows. Surveyed in Chapter 13, not run.1318
MemRL
A research prototype in which feedback changes each stored episode's utility score while the model's weights stay frozen. It needs feedback or judge calls, and a false-positive reward can contaminate scores. Surveyed in Chapter 16, not run.0616
memU
A beta memory service for a shared Markdown wiki and agent-authored skills, with local SQLite, Postgres or cloud storage.01021316
Metadata filter payload filter
A stored-field condition, such as user, project or date. In hybrid search, apply it inside each search leg before merging.0511
MEX
A local command-line tool (0.9.0-beta.1.1, MIT) that holds back project notes whose code checks fail and shares reviewed Markdown notes in git. Anonymous usage telemetry is on by default. Not run.0113
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service Memory
Microsoft's managed agent memory, in public preview as of 20 November 2026. It keeps user-profile, chat-summary and procedural memory per scope, with a default TTL. Chapter 13 describes its setup from docs, not run.1318
Minimum necessary
A health-privacy principle: use or share only the least patient information the purpose needs. Chapter 22 turns it into field allowlists for each task.22
MINJA
An attack that plants malicious records in an agent's memory through ordinary queries, with no write access to the store.001617
MLX
A toolkit for running models on Apple Silicon. Its server is OpenAI-compatible, but its guide says not to use it in production.0610
MMEB Massive Multimodal Embedding Benchmark
A benchmark for image, video and document embeddings; its second version, MMEB-V2, has 78 tasks.04
mmproj
See Vision projector.
MMR maximal marginal relevance
A method picking results individually, favoring notes relevant to the query and unlike those already chosen.05
MMTEB Massive Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark
The multilingual extension of MTEB. Chapter 03 reports model scores on it.0304
Modality
A kind of input: text, image, video or audio.04
Modality gap
The tendency of text and image vectors to sit in separate regions of the space even when their meanings match.04
MRL Matryoshka representation learning
Training that makes the first k numbers of a vector usable alone. Shorten vectors only for a model trained for it, and only to sizes its card lists.03
MRR mean reciprocal rank
Per question, score 1/rank of the first correct hit, or 0 if none; average over all questions. For MRR@k, count only hits in the first k.05
MTEB Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
A public suite, in several versions, that scores text embedding models on retrieval, clustering and similar tasks.03
Multi-hop question
A question whose answer needs two or more edges in a row.14
Multi-vector
Keeping several vectors per item, such as token or page-patch vectors. The late-interaction examples use MaxSim. See Late interaction and ColPali and the ColQwen family.03040511

N

Namespace
A label that partitions records inside a store or collection, often one per tenant. It is not a security boundary alone: enforce tenant scope in every query and test cross-tenant reads. See LangGraph.1113
nDCG normalized discounted cumulative gain
A score that rewards correct results more when they rank higher, scaled so a perfect ordering scores 1.05
Neo4j
A graph database queried through Cypher.14
Node, edge
A graph node represents a thing, such as a person or company; an edge links two nodes with a relationship or fact.14

O

Observational memory
Mastra's approach, in which a background agent writes dated observations about a thread and a second step condenses them; it suits long-running threads.13
OCR optical character recognition
Software that reads text out of page images. Page-image retrieval is compared against OCR, which can lose layout.04
Ollama
A program running local models through an API. Its format field accepts a JSON schema, and "think": false switches thinking off.02030607
openCypher
See Cypher.
OpenViking
An open-source context database from Volcengine. It presents knowledge, memory and skills as one virtual filesystem with three levels per directory (see L0, L1, L2).0218
Outbox pattern transactional outbox
A pattern that commits a source change and its pending work in one database transaction. A worker builds the searchable copy later; delivery can repeat safely if consumers are idempotent.0817212223
OWASP Open Worldwide Application Security Project
A security group whose agentic-applications list names memory and context poisoning as ASI06. Its separate list for LLM applications includes LLM08, Vector and Embedding Weaknesses, which covers leakage between users of a shared vector database.17

P

Parameter weight
A learned number inside a model. Model size counts parameters; quantization stores weights in fewer bits.030607
Parametric memory
Knowledge in model weights, versus text in an outside store.1516
Payload
Metadata saved beside a vector, such as a user id or timestamp.11
PBX private branch exchange
The phone switch of an office. It takes calls from the carrier, plays greetings and offers a human.2223
Pending correction
In Chapter 12's materializer, a correction whose parent has not arrived. It stays unpublished and unsearchable until every ancestor arrives.12
PerLTQA
See xMemory.
Personalized PageRank
HippoRAG's ranking method: repeatedly pass score to neighboring nodes, restarting often at query entities, to favor nearby nodes.14
pgvector
A Postgres extension that adds vector types, distance operators and HNSW and IVFFlat indexes, so Postgres can store embeddings and find the nearest rows.081118
PHI protected health information
Health information that identifies a patient and falls under HIPAA. Chapter 22 limits which fields a model call may see.22
Pipecat
An open-source real-time voice framework connecting STT, a model and TTS. Proposed with AudioSocket in Chapters 22 and 23, not run.
Policy gateway
A program between models and tools. It checks the subject (patient, customer or project), task and policy, runs only allowlisted tools and records every read and write in the audit trail.2223
Post-filtering
Searching then dropping non-matching hits, potentially leaving fewer than k results. Without iterative scan, Postgres WHERE filters only the fixed batch fetched by a pgvector ANN scan; iterative scan keeps walking the index (see Iterative scan).0811
PostgreSQL Postgres
An open-source relational database (Chapters 08, 11, 18). See ACID, GIN, RLS, pgvector and Apache AGE.
Prefill
The step where a model reads the whole prompt before writing its first token. Prompt caches and KV-cache offload save prefill work, not new-token generation.1022
Pre-filtering
Applying the filter before the approximate search, so the search considers only allowed vectors.11
Prefix cache inference-level reuse
A local inference engine keeps or restores a prompt prefix's KV cache, so a repeated prefix is not read again.1019
Prefix (embedding)
A short instruction before text that some models expect on queries, documents or both. Follow the model card for each side; omission silently lowers quality.03
Prefix (prompt)
The start of a prompt; two requests share a prefix when their first tokens match.1019
Procedural memory
How to do things: rules, instructions and skills, usually kept in versioned files such as CLAUDE.md or a skills folder.0016
Projection
A worker-built searchable copy of source records: rows, vectors and indexes. Only a current projection may enter a prompt (Chapter 17).1720
Prompt cache provider prompt caching
The provider keeps the KV cache for a repeated prefix and bills the re-read at a lower rate.0010
Prompt injection
Untrusted content that carries instructions the model may obey. Chapter 17 describes such content writing instructions into a memory that later chats read.17
Property graph
A graph whose nodes and edges carry named fields. Neo4j and FalkorDB are examples.14
Purpose-trained memory writer
A model trained to select, represent and reconcile information for persistent external memory. A general model given an extraction prompt is different.0616

Q

QAT quantization-aware training
Training a compressed model to work at low precision, instead of converting a finished checkpoint.06
Qdrant
A vector store written in Rust that filters by payload with indexes and supports late interaction with a MaxSim comparator.0411
qmd
A local search tool for a wiki that combines BM25, vector search and LLM reranking, with a command-line tool and an MCP server.02
Quantization (model)
Storing a model's weights with fewer bits, such as 4, so the model needs less memory.06
Quantization (vector)
Storing each number of a vector in fewer bits, such as 8-bit integers or single bits, to shrink it.0311
Query rewriting
An LLM call that turns a follow-up such as "and the other one?" into a standalone question using the last few turns.05
Qwen3.8-Max License
The license on Qwen/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B and its FP8 build (card license: other, license_name: qwen3.8-max), read 20 November 2026. The Qwen3.8 27B models use Apache-2.0, so licenses differ by model.0607

R

RAG retrieval-augmented generation
A text generator combined with a retriever, so the model can use knowledge outside its weights. It retrieves, then generates.00141516
RAPTOR
A tree of summaries instead of an entity graph: it embeds chunks, clusters them, summarizes each cluster, then retrieves across levels. See Chapter 05, Hierarchical summary-tree retrieval (RAPTOR).0514
Raw source
An original article, paper or note stored unchanged; agents read, never edit it.02
RDB snapshot
A point-in-time Redis disk copy. The directive save 60 1000 takes a snapshot after at least 60 seconds and at least 1000 changes.09
RDF resource description framework
A model that stores facts as subject-predicate-object triples with shared identifiers. Ontologies define the vocabulary, and a compatible reasoner can infer facts.14
Readiness loop
A bounded retry loop that polls the exact endpoint the next command uses (curl --fail for HTTP, pg_isready plus one query for Postgres), prints the service logs on timeout and stops. It replaces a fixed sleep.020308
Read path
The steps that bring the right part of memory back into the window: decide to recall, search, rank and inject.00
Recall
1. The read path, or a read call that brings memories back. 2. The metric: of all the correct results that exist, the share the search returns. For approximate search, compare returned neighbors with the exact top k; tune search settings against speed.0508
Recall@k
The share of all known-correct notes that appear in the top k results: 3 of 4 correct notes in the top 10 gives recall@10 of 0.75.0517
Receipt
A durable write-acceptance record. Retrying the same idempotency key and payload returns the earlier receipt. Acceptance does not mean searchability. Protect and expire receipts.172223
Recorded time transaction time
When a version was in the store, from recorded_at to superseded_at.142223
Recursive language model
A research method that treats a long prompt as a variable the model inspects with code and calls itself on in pieces.16
Redis
An in-memory data server with hashes, lists, streams, sorted sets and self-deleting keys. It can serve as a hot tier (see Hot tier).091018
RedisVL
A Python client for Redis that provides SearchIndex, VectorQuery and SemanticCache.0910
Reference design
A worked design to adapt, not an installation guide or professional advice. Chapters 21 to 23 are reference designs.212223
Refusal
A response that declines the extraction task; a missing fact alone is an omission, not refusal.07
Request hash
A fingerprint of tenant, memory id, operation and payload, stored with the idempotency key (the event id in Chapter 17). A retry with a matching hash returns the earlier receipt; a different payload under the same idempotency key is rejected.1721
Reranker
A model that rescores the best candidates and reorders them. It cannot add notes outside the candidate pool.040519
Retain, recall, reflect
Hindsight's three calls. Retain saves a note, recall fetches related notes and reflect asks the model to reason over them.061319
RLS row-level security
Database policies filtering readable or writable rows through a per-row predicate. Enable RLS and test as the application role: a non-owner without superuser or BYPASSRLS privileges. Owners bypass policies unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY applies. Retain application query filtering; cover every reachable table and give cross-tenant workers separate roles.082223
RRF reciprocal rank fusion
A method that merges ranked lists using 1-based rank: each list gives a note 1 / (k + rank), then scores add. Here k is a smoothing constant, not top-k; the book uses k = 60 as an example.05081219
Runtime utility learning
Raising or lowering a stored memory's score by whether using it helped, without changing weights. MemRL does this for episodic memories.0616
Run token
A value tying lab cleanup to its run, preventing removal of folders created elsewhere. Lab scripts refuse existing lab paths before writing.02030507081020

S

Schema
In the wiki, a file such as AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md that states the page format and the ingest, query and lint steps. Elsewhere (Chapters 06 and 07), JSON describing required output fields and types; see Structured output and Constrained decoding.02
SDK software development kit
A vendor library for calling its service from code.0113
Semantic cache
A cache that matches a new question to an earlier one by meaning instead of exact text. Match tenant, permissions and data version exactly first; recompute doubtful hits.10
Semantic memory
Facts and preferences distilled from experience, no longer tied to one event, kept in indexed rows, a knowledge graph or wiki pages.00
Shadow index
A new index built with a new embedding model beside the old one. Run the golden set on both, switch by alias and keep the old index until the new one passes.17
Similarity threshold distance threshold
The cutoff for treating two texts as a match: a minimum similarity or, equivalently, a maximum distance.10
SIP Session Initiation Protocol
The standard that sets up phone calls over IP; the audio usually travels over RTP (Real-time Transport Protocol). A SIP trunk is a carrier's line into the PBX and remains an outside service.2223
Skill
A reusable procedure kept as a file or folder that an agent can load. It is part of procedural memory.00011619
SkillJack
A reported attack (August 2026) in which the agent's own extraction rewrites a poisoned experience into a clean-looking skill that stays active after the source is deleted.1617
Sleep-time agent
In Letta, a second agent that edits the main agent's memory blocks in the background while the main agent is idle.0616
Sleep-time compute
Letting a model think about stored context while no user waits and write down likely questions and derived facts, so answers are cheaper later.16
Soft forgetting retrieval-strength decay
Lowering retrieval strength without erasing stored evidence. Verified use may reinforce that strength. It does not make a memory true or override authorization, expiry or erasure. See Chapter 05, Soft forgetting.0516
Source-linked raw evidence
Original messages or tool output kept behind explicit links from compact notes, so the notes can be checked.16
SPARQL SPARQL Protocol and RDF Query Language
A language for querying RDF triples.14
Sparse vector
A vector with a slot per vocabulary term, mostly zero; non-zero weights mark important terms. Learned models such as SPLADE also weight related terms absent from the text. A shared term scores only if both vectors retain its weight. Its size depends on the non-zero term count and the index encoding.0305
SPLADE
A learned sparse model that keeps the inverted-index form of keyword search but uses a model to expand each text with related terms.05
SQLite
A database in one ordinary file, running inside its host program without a server.000512
sqlite-vec
A SQLite extension that stores and searches vectors. It is pre-v1, so pin the version.05111218
STATE-Bench
A Microsoft benchmark (May 2026) of 450 customer-support, travel and shopping tasks scored against deterministic end-state checks, five runs per task.16
Stream (Redis)
An append-only log of entries with ids, read by position or by a group of workers.09
Structured output
A model answer in a fixed machine-readable format such as JSON that code can parse. Graphiti depends on it.06
STT speech to text
Turning audio into text. The case studies propose Whisper large-v3-turbo (MIT) through a local runtime.212223
Sufficiency routing
Deciding whether retrieved compact notes hold enough evidence for a question, and escalating to source-linked raw history if not.16
Summary tree
The structure RAPTOR builds at write time: source chunks at the bottom, a model-written summary of each cluster above them, repeating up to a root. Each summary traces back to its chunks.05
Supermemory
A hosted memory product that keeps extracted memories and user profiles. Its repository is MIT-licensed.13
Superseded
Marked as no longer current while the record is kept instead of deleted.001214
System prompt
The instructions the harness sends to the model ahead of the conversation. In Claude Code, CLAUDE.md content arrives as a user message after the system prompt, not inside it.0001

T

Tamper evidence
Detecting unauthorized changes to stored memory using an append-only hash-chained log, signed writes and verification on read and restore. It does not show an authorized write was true or safe. Chapter 17 tested a keyed hash chain locally; the other controls are proposed.17
Task and dependency memory
Memory of what is left to do, what blocks what, who has taken an item and where work stopped. A task store such as Beads holds it; a notes file does not.000118
TCPA Telephone Consumer Protection Act
The US law that limits automated calls and texts. Chapter 22 keeps outbound AI voice off until counsel verifies the current rule.22
TEI text-embeddings-inference
A Hugging Face server for running embedding models. Chapter 03 runs it on CPU.03
Temporal graph
A knowledge graph whose facts carry validity windows, so changed facts are invalidated instead of deleted.001314
Tenant
One customer or user group whose data must stay separate from other tenants. Embeddings, outbox receipts and cache keys belong to a tenant too and are never shared.001117
TencentDB Agent Memory
A self-run, MIT-licensed memory that layers raw dialogue, atomic facts, scenarios, profiles and skills, with source drill-down and SQLite plus sqlite-vec by default. Surveyed in Chapter 13, not run.13
Test-time memory
A small neural module updated while a model reads, so it memorizes what it sees. See Titans.16
Thinking mode
A model setting that writes reasoning before answering. Chapter 06 recommends disabling it for schema-constrained extraction: reasoning can exhaust the output limit before JSON starts.0619
Third-party facts
Facts about other people, such as names, health and relationships. Exclude or redact them at write time unless policy permits retention for the stated purpose; the speaker's preference alone is not authorization (Chapter 07).07
TierMem
A research memory with two linked tiers, compact notes and original interaction pages. A trained router checks whether the notes hold enough evidence and, if not, follows links to the raw pages. MIT-licensed code. Not run.16
Titans
A Google paper on test-time memory: attention stays short-term memory, and an added module updates while the model reads.16
Token
A word piece, the unit of text a model reads; context windows are counted in tokens.0003
Tombstone
A durable delete event that stops old data from reappearing after replay, sync or restore.12172223
Top-k
The k best-ranked results kept after a search.051115
tsvector
A Postgres type that stores a text's words for keyword search. It is indexed with GIN and ranked with ts_rank.08
TTL time to live
How long a key may live before it expires and stops being returned. In Redis, set it with EXPIRE or SET with EX or PX.0910
TTS text to speech
Turning text into audio. Chapter 22 proposes Kokoro and Chapter 23 a Qwen3 model, and neither is run. Chapter 23 leaves Arabic voice approval unresolved.2223
Turn detection
Deciding when a caller has finished speaking. Chapter 22 proposes Smart Turn v3, an 8 MB model on the CPU, for this; the audio path is from docs, not run.2223
Two timelines
See Bitemporal.

U

Upsert
A write that inserts a record or replaces the existing one with the same key.1117

V

Valid time validity window
When a claim applies in the world, as the interval [valid_from, valid_to), where the start is included and the end is not, as in Chapters 08 and 21 to 23 (Chapter 14's invalid_at is the same exclusive end).0814212223
Valkey
A community fork of Redis with the same protocol, still BSD-licensed. Its core image has no search.091018
vec0
The virtual table type that the sqlite-vec extension adds for storing vectors.12
Vector
An embedding's number list; its length is its dimension count.0304
Vector search dense search
Finds the stored embeddings nearest to the query. It suits paraphrases and loose wording but is weak on exact terms.0005
Vector store
An embedding-centered database returning the nearest stored vectors and their metadata to a query vector.11
Version-evolution chain diff chain
Linked code revisions and their diffs, preserving changes that a later edit or revert can hide from the working tree. Hy-Memory stores the chain without model calls.0616
ViDoRe
A benchmark for retrieving from page images, introduced by the ColPali authors. ViDoRe V3 has 10 datasets, about 26,000 pages and 6 languages.0418
Vision projector mmproj
A separate set of weights that turns image features into tokens a language model reads. In GGUF packaging it is a file beside the model, so Chapter 06's Qwen3.5 9B download sizes differ with and without it.0621
vLLM
A server with an OpenAI-compatible API, continuous batching and matching prompt-prefix KV-cache reuse reducing prefill work. Chapters 22 and 23 propose it for GPU serving.0610
VLM vision-language model
A model that reads images as well as text, for example to write captions. In Chapter 02, OpenViking's vlm setting names the chat model writing directory summaries.02
VPN virtual private network
An encrypted tunnel that lets devices reach a private service without exposing it publicly.21

W

WAL write-ahead logging
A SQLite journal mode that lets readers continue while one writer commits. Chapter 12 describes its rare reset-race bug and the fixing version.051217
Whisper
A speech recognition model family. The case studies propose large-v3-turbo through faster-whisper or whisper.cpp.212223
Working memory
What the model is handling right now: the live conversation, tool results and a scratchpad.00
Worktree
A git feature that checks out a branch in its own folder, so agents can work in parallel.01
WorldMemArena
A benchmark (May 2026) of 400 multi-session multimodal tasks for agents that see and act.16
Write path
The steps that save what happened: capture, extract, store, consolidate and forget.00

X

xMemory
A research prototype that splits interaction history into events and reusable memory components, and retrieves from grouped components down to the original messages when needed. Its authors report results on LoCoMo and PerLTQA (a personal long-term question-answering benchmark).16

Z

Zep
A hosted memory service built on open-source Graphiti; the two are distinct products.1314

Appendix B

Attached files

The 144 files below are attached to this PDF: 141 code files from the chapter walkthroughs and 3 large map images under maps/. The same files are in the companion repository, one folder per chapter named like the attachment prefix, with the maps under maps/. The repository address and the command that copies all of it:

https://github.com/shoemoney/Ai_Memory
git clone https://github.com/shoemoney/Ai_Memory.git

The chapters cite each code file by its label. Every source link in the book, by chapter and number, is also listed in the companion repository under sources/.

To open the attachments, look for a paperclip icon or an Attachments entry in the side panel of your PDF reader and save the files from there. If your reader lists none, extract them with pymupdf:

import pymupdf, pathlib
doc = pymupdf.open("ai-memory-guide.pdf")
for name in doc.embfile_names():
    target = pathlib.Path("attachments") / name
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    target.write_bytes(doc.embfile_get(name))
